sections.h2: What is Lamar County, Georgia known for?
sections.html:
Lamar County lies between Atlanta and Macon, and Barnesville is its seat. Barnesville was settled in 1826, and its leaders petitioned the legislature in 1869, 1906, 1912 and 1916 before the county finally came into being in 1920, cut from Monroe and Pike counties. The result is about 185 square miles of rolling land whose streams run to the Flint and Ocmulgee rivers.

The town earned the title Buggy Capital of the South. One factory predicted in 1897 that it would ship at least 1,200 buggies, and a September Buggy Days parade still shows off original Barnesville buggies. Gordon State College, founded in 1872 as Gordon Institute and a four-year school since 2007, fills out the town's profile, and the Barnesville Expo Center joins a wetlands trail to a livestock arena. Pecan and peach groves cover the farmland.

The population stood at 9,745 in 1930, reached 18,317 in 2010 and 18,500 in 2020. Land area is 183.50 square miles, so the county packs 100.8 residents into each one, the highest density among the four counties compared here.

sections.h2: How fast is Lamar County growing, and what does it mean for prices?
sections.html:
Census estimates have Lamar County adding 13.2% to its population between April 2020 and July 2025, far ahead of Johnson, Jones or Lanier.

At $216,500, the median owner-home value is the highest of the four counties. A 136-permit year means newer houses compete with resale listings, and the 31.8-minute commute is the longest of the four. Sellers with an older house should expect buyers to compare it with that new supply.

sections.h2: What does the Lamar County economy add to the housing picture?
sections.html:
Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,469, versus $526 for those without, and the median gross rent is $878. Households average 2.60 people, 92.5% of residents were in the same house a year earlier, and 7,133 households were counted.

Employers numbered 275 in 2023, supporting 3,775 jobs (up 10.1% over 2022) and $174,423 thousand in payroll, and 1,922 nonemployer businesses were counted in 2024. Retail sales were $150,591 thousand in 2022, which works out to $7,733 per resident, and transportation and warehousing took in $20,621 thousand, almost as much as health care and social assistance at $22,229 thousand. Another $23,100 thousand came from accommodation and food service. About 56.7% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, 89.6% of adults 25 and older finished high school, and 19.2% hold a bachelor's degree. Poverty is 12.6%, and 1,320 residents are veterans.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Lamar County property tax questions?
sections.html:
Most of this runs through Barnesville, and the details below come from the county's tax pages.

  • Tax Commissioner: 790 Veteran's Pkwy, Barnesville, GA 30204; mail to P.O. Box 850; phone (770) 358-5162. The lobby takes customers Monday to Thursday from 8 until 4:30 and Friday until 4:15, and the drive-thru stops about a quarter hour sooner each day.
  • Tax Assessor, (770) 358-5161: values and appeals. Homestead forms are filed here, Monday to Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday 8 to 4.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the courthouse deed room, for a copy of a warranty deed.

The commissioner's website accepts online payment of property tax and car tag renewals. It also explains that the commissioner neither sets values nor chooses millage, so an objection to a high figure belongs at the assessor's counter.

sections.h2: When are Lamar County taxes due, and what happens after?
sections.html:
Lamar bills usually leave by September 15 and are due November 15, a calendar the county says began with the 2018 tax year. That is well ahead of Georgia's December 20 default, which trips up owners who moved from other counties.

  • Interest runs at 1% a month on real estate and business personal property once the due date passes.
  • A 10% penalty is added to amounts still unpaid after 90 days.
  • The county's FAQ says a fifa lien can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court when taxes are more than 30 days late, and credit bureaus can pick up the public record.
  • Mobile homes fall due April 1, with a 10% filing penalty plus 1% a month, and an unpaid home can be sold at auction.

State guidance also gives each taxpayer 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest, so keep the envelope. Money paid in error can be reclaimed by a written request started within three years.

sections.h2: Which Lamar County homestead exemptions can I file for?
sections.html:
Forms are accepted from January 1 through April 1, and the county says Georgia allows no extension: a missed window waives the exemption for that year. Approved exemptions renew automatically. Bring a driver license and either a 1040 or a signed income affidavit.

  • State types carry codes: S1 regular homestead, S3 elderly at 62, L4 elderly at 65, S5 disabled veteran and SS surviving spouse of a veteran, the last two requiring VA proof of 100% service-connected disability.
  • Local county break for owners over 65: $20,000 off county maintenance and operation only.
  • Local school break for owners over 70: $7,000 off school maintenance and operation and school bonds.
  • Local disability break: $15,000 off school maintenance and operation, when a couple's household income is under $20,000, backed by two physicians' letters or a Social Security letter declaring 100% disability.

Local breaks apply only after the state requirements are met. Homeowners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less may also defer tax under the state program. A mobile home can qualify only if the same person owns the home and the land beneath it.

sections.h2: How does a Lamar County owner appeal a value?
sections.html:
Appraisers set values from recent sales and market conditions as of January 1, and notices usually go out in spring. Forty-five days from the notice date is the limit for contesting taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. The written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and must say which route you choose, and the Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears the administrative cases.

Land owners have extra programs. Lamar's page lists conservation use and residential transitional property under Georgia Code section 48-5-7.4, agricultural property under 48-5-7.4.1 and rehabilitated historic property under 48-5-7.2, each demanding a covenant of at least 10 years. Anyone selling enrolled acreage should ask the assessors what happens to the covenant when the deed changes hands.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Lamar County house with taxes still owed?
sections.html:
Ask the commissioner for a payoff that includes interest and penalty, and confirm with the Clerk whether a fifa has been recorded. The closing agent can pay from the proceeds and secure the release. Whoever owns the property on January 1 owes that year's bill, which is why contracts usually prorate it.

If the owner has died, ask the county Probate Court how to open the estate before anyone lists the house. A buyer paying cash in Barnesville or the rural parts will still want the payoff handled at closing.

faqs.q: When must Lamar County owners pay their property tax?
faqs.a: By November 15, with bills normally mailed by September 15. Mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How much extra does Lamar County charge for late tax?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% a month starts after the due date, and 10% is added after 90 days. The FAQ says a lien can be recorded at 30 days.

faqs.q: Do Lamar County seniors get a local exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners over 65 get $20,000 off county maintenance and operation, and owners over 70 get $7,000 off school maintenance and operation and school bonds, once state requirements are met.

faqs.q: What is a Lamar County house worth at the median?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts it at $216,500 for 2020-2024, with 20,941 residents estimated in July 2025.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead in Lamar County?
faqs.a: At the Tax Assessor's office between January 1 and April 1, with a driver license and a 1040 or signed income affidavit.
